messages:
Maya Kapoor: Quick heads-up — profiling run on branch batch-tune-2026 shows a perf regression on A100 after bumping max_tokens_per_batch to 64k. p95 jump for long seqs. attaching notes.
Arjun Singh: Saw that. p50 up ~12% at seq=2048, p95 worse. Kernel selector fell back in a few hotspots — looks like cuBLAS->generic in places.
Leo Park: Confirmed. Selector chose fp16-cuBLAS for most matmuls but for KV gather it fell back to the generic kernel when kv_fragmentation > ~2.8.
Priya Nair: KV cache stats: with 64k per-batch tokens, cache hit rate on A100 dropped 92% -> 76%. Packing crosses shard boundaries and we lose locality.
Dan O'Hara: Proposal: bind max_tokens_per_batch to device mem + kernel frag heuristic. Initial suggested targets (device-budget tokens / max_batch_size caps):
- L4: max_tokens 18k, max_batch_size 64
- T4: max_tokens 12k, max_batch_size 48
- A10: max_tokens 28k, max_batch_size 80
- A100: max_tokens 40k, max_batch_size 128
- H100: max_tokens 60k, max_batch_size 160
Maya Kapoor: Those look sensible as a starting point. Need to validate latency vs cost and ensure selector switches to packed-kv kernel when frag < 2. Also want dynamic fallback if p95 > SLO.
Arjun Singh: Ran microbench with the targets above. Quick paste:
```text
model: rwft-13b
seq=1024: A100 p95 baseline=210ms, new=195ms
seq=2048: A100 p95 baseline=470ms, new=510ms  <-- regression
```
So smaller seq improved but long sequences regressed.
Leo Park: Hypothesis: for seq >= 1536, large token budgets force too many per-request KV pages, increasing scatter and sync overhead. Suggest reducing A100 max_tokens_per_batch by 25% for seq>=1536.
Priya Nair: Agreed. Also we should surface a runtime metric "kv.fragmentation" and a per-request tag so we can correlate p95 spikes to fragmentation in the console.
Dan O'Hara: Queue policy change: make admission token-budget aware. Pseudocode:
```python
if queued_tokens + req_tokens > device_budget:
    route_to_fallback()  # lower-capacity model / different region
else:
    admit_request()
```
This avoids oversubscribing and large tail latencies.
Maya Kapoor: Can someone draft a short RFC with the per-GPU numbers + kernel-selector rule + queue policy? Add a CI perf gate that runs the full seq sweep (512/1024/1536/2048) before merge.
Arjun Singh: I'll open PR today with the per-gpu config map and the benchmark harness. Adding flag `runtime.batch.max_tokens_profile = {"A100":40000,...}` and tuned kernel thresholds.
infra-bot: Perf CI started for branch batch-tune-2026 — build 8421, estimated time ~45m.
Leo Park: FYI H100 shows odd thermal/clock throttling on a couple of hosts when tensor cores run high-util mixed-precision on very big batches. We might need host-level thermal metrics in experiments.
Priya Nair: Another mitigation: increase pack window for A100 from 10ms -> 20ms to improve packing locality. Might raise median a bit but reduce tail.
Dan O'Hara: Let's run an A/B: A = window=10ms + current caps, B = window=20ms + reduced A100 cap for seq>=1536. Compare cost, p50, p95.
Maya Kapoor: Timeline: Arjun PR today; Leo/Priya targeted perf runs tomorrow; Dan update queue policy; I'll draft RFC and sync Fri. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Perf CI finished for build 8421 — results uploaded (internal link). Preliminary: regressions flagged on A100 for seq>=1536. See CI comments.
Arjun Singh: Got the CI link, investigating kernel fallback traces and kv.fragmentation correlation. Will report back with narrowed repro steps.
Maya Kapoor: Thanks everyone. Keep notes in the PR and add any small graphs to the perf clipboard. If we see infra thermal noise on H100, tag hosts in the run so ops can follow up.
